meta.titre: The Coniferous Forest Ecosystem: cold-climate trees, thin soils and timber for paper
meta.sous_theme: Climate, vegetation, soils and uses of the coniferous forest

sections.contenu_markdown: The great coniferous forest biome does not occur in Cameroon, yet the paper in an exercise book may well have started as wood from one. Far to the north of the equator, huge forests of cone-bearing trees cover cold lands and supply much of the world's softwood. The GCE paper tests where this biome is found, how its trees cope with winter, and how it compares with the tropical rainforest. Learn it as a chain from climate to trees, soil and human use.

items: Evergreen trees keep leaves all year, while deciduous trees lose them in the cold or dry season.
Latitude shows how far a place is from the equator, and high latitudes are colder.
A biome is a very large ecosystem identified by its dominant vegetation.
Photosynthesis needs light and warmth, so growth slows in the cold.

sections.titre: Coniferous forest: climate, adaptations, soil and uses
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Where and what
The **coniferous forest** (also called the **taiga** or boreal forest) forms a broad belt in the northern parts of North America, Europe and Asia, mostly between about 50° N and 65° N. Examples are northern Canada, Scandinavia and Siberia.

### Climate
Winters are long and very cold, with temperatures well below freezing for months. Summers are short, and cool to mild. Precipitation is low to moderate and much of it falls as snow. The growing season is short.

### Adaptations of the trees
| Feature | How it helps |
|---|---|
| Narrow needle leaves with a waxy coat | Cut water loss when the ground is frozen and resist frost |
| Cone-shaped tree, flexible branches slope downwards | Snow slides off and branches do not break |
| Evergreen leaves | Trees photosynthesise as soon as it is warm enough, without regrowing leaves |
| Shallow spreading roots | Reach the thin thawed soil and anchor the tree |
| Thick bark | Protects against cold and fire |

The forest is often made up of **few species**, such as pine, spruce and fir, growing in dense **pure stands** with little undergrowth because the dark canopy blocks light.

### Soil and animals
Needle litter is acid and decays slowly in the cold, so the humus layer is thin. Rain and melting snow wash minerals downwards, leaving poor, acid **podzol** soils. Animals include wolves, bears, lynx and moose, and many have thick fur or hibernate in winter.

### Human use
Trees are cut for **softwood** timber, pulp and paper, and furniture. Large-scale felling, forest fires and clearing cause loss of habitat and need careful management.

variantes.nom: Comparing coniferous forest and tropical rainforest
variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks for similarities or differences
variantes.contenu_markdown: Similar: both are forests of tall trees with dense canopies, both look green all year because the trees never lose all their leaves at one time, and both are cut for timber. Different: rainforest has hundreds of broad-leaved species in layers, hot and wet climate, fast decay and hardwoods; coniferous forest has few needle-leaved species, a cold climate, slow decay and softwoods.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the command is explain how the trees survive
variantes.contenu_markdown: Name the feature and then say what problem it solves: *needle leaves with a waxy coat* (feature), *reduce water loss when the soil is frozen* (use). One feature without its purpose earns few marks.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks about the use of the forest
variantes.contenu_markdown: Give the product (softwood, pulp, paper, furniture), the reason it is easy to exploit (trees are straight and grow close together in single-species stands) and one problem (loss of habitat or damage to soils).

sections.enonce_markdown: Explain how the trees of the coniferous forest are adapted to the cold climate. (6 marks)

etapes.justification: An adaptation answer must match features to problems.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Long frozen winters, heavy snow, thin soils.

etapes.action: Match needles to the water problem.
etapes.justification: Frozen ground limits water, so leaves must lose little.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Needle leaves with a waxy coat reduce water loss.

etapes.action: Match shape to the snow problem.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Cone shape and downward-sloping flexible branches let snow slide off.

etapes.action: Match evergreen leaves to the short growing season.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Trees can photosynthesise as soon as it is warm enough.

etapes.justification: A further feature secures full marks.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Shallow roots exploit thin soil; thick bark protects against cold.

sections.conclusion_markdown: Model answer: The trees have narrow needle leaves with a waxy coat, which reduces water loss when the ground is frozen. Their cone shape and flexible, downward-sloping branches let heavy snow slide off without breaking them. They are evergreen, so they can photosynthesise as soon as the weather warms in the short summer, without having to grow new leaves. Shallow, spreading roots make use of the thin layer of soil that thaws, and thick bark protects the trees against cold.

items.erreur_markdown: Writing that coniferous trees lose all their leaves in autumn like oak.
items.pourquoi_faux: Most conifers are evergreen; the oak is a deciduous tree.
items.correction_markdown: Write that conifers keep their needles all year, while deciduous trees such as oak shed their leaves.

items.erreur_markdown: Saying the needle leaves help the tree to catch more sunlight.
items.pourquoi_faux: Narrow needles have a small surface, and their main use is to reduce water loss.
items.correction_markdown: Say that needles with a waxy coat reduce water loss and resist frost.

items.erreur_markdown: Describing the forest as having many species in several layers.
items.pourquoi_faux: That description fits the tropical rainforest. Coniferous forest has few species and a simple structure.
items.correction_markdown: Say that it consists of a few species such as pine and spruce, with little undergrowth.

items.erreur_markdown: Placing the coniferous forest near the equator or in Cameroon.
items.pourquoi_faux: The forest needs a cold climate, so it lies in high northern latitudes.
items.correction_markdown: Locate it in northern Canada, Scandinavia or Siberia.

items.erreur_markdown: Describing the soil as rich because of the deep layer of leaf litter.
items.pourquoi_faux: Needles are acid and decay slowly in the cold, so the soil is thin, acid and poor.
items.correction_markdown: Write that the soil is a poor, acid podzol with a thin humus layer.

items.enonce_markdown: State three features of the climate of the coniferous forest.
items.solution_markdown:
Any three of the following earn full marks:
- Winters are long and very cold.
- Summers are short and cool to mild.
- Precipitation is low to moderate, much of it as snow.
- The growing season is short.

**Three correct features earn full marks.**

items.enonce_markdown:
Station Z lies in a coniferous forest.

| Month | J | F | M | A | M | J | J | A | S | O | N | D |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Temperature (°C) | -22 | -20 | -12 | -2 | 6 | 12 | 16 | 13 | 7 | 0 | -12 | -19 |
| Precipitation (mm) | 30 | 25 | 25 | 25 | 35 | 50 | 70 | 65 | 50 | 45 | 40 | 35 |

Calculate (a) the annual temperature range, (b) the number of months with a mean temperature below 0 °C, and (c) the total annual precipitation.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) Range = 16 - (-22) = **38 °C**.

(b) The months below 0 °C are January, February, March, April, November and December, so the number is **6 months**.

(c) Total = 30 + 25 + 25 + 25 + 35 + 50 + 70 + 65 + 50 + 45 + 40 + 35 = **495 mm**.

Cold winters, a short growing season and moderate precipitation are typical of a coniferous forest.

items.enonce_markdown: Explain why coniferous forests are easier to exploit commercially than tropical rainforests, and state one problem caused by heavy exploitation. (5 marks)
items.solution_markdown:
Award marks for points such as:
- Coniferous forests are often pure stands of one or a few species, so the same kind of timber can be cut over a large area.
- Softwood trees are straight and similar in size, so they are easy to cut, transport and process into planks, pulp and paper.
- Tropical rainforest contains very many species mixed together, and the valuable trees are scattered, so logging is slower and more costly.
- Problem: large-scale felling destroys wildlife habitat, exposes soils and can lead to erosion if replanting is not carried out.

**Explained reasons plus one explained problem earn full marks.**

items_markdown: Coniferous forest (taiga) lies in high northern latitudes such as northern Canada, Scandinavia and Siberia.
The climate has long, very cold winters, short cool summers and moderate precipitation, much of it snow.
Needle leaves, cone shape, evergreen foliage, shallow roots and thick bark are adaptations to the cold.
The forest has few species, dense pure stands, little undergrowth and poor acid podzol soils.
It supplies softwood, pulp and paper, but heavy felling destroys habitats.
Compare with the rainforest: both are green and tall; the rainforest has many species, hardwoods and a hot wet climate.
